Lists that take sites, addresses and programs, a Forbidden list, three auto-switch modes, presets you edit, and a Live page you route from.

To update, run the new `dpiswitch.exe` from anywhere and accept the offer to install over the installed version (one administrator prompt). Settings, lists, configs and verdicts are kept.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Observe only now sends everything direct.** It used to send everything through the tunnel; that is the new **Tunnel only** mode. If auto-switch was off (Observe only) before the update, it comes up as Tunnel only, so your traffic stays in the tunnel; choose Observe only yourself only if you want everything direct.

## Routing lists

- **Always direct, Always via tunnel and the second tunnel's own list each take sites, addresses and programs** in one box, in any mix: `example.com`, `+.example.com`, `192.168.0.0/16`, `C:\Games\game.exe`. The service splits every list for the core by kind; an address matches only a connection made by address.
- **A new Forbidden list:** what it names is refused in every mode. The detector never probes a forbidden site, and Live shows the refused tries.
- The old "Programs bypassing the tunnel" list is taken into Always direct, until that list is next saved.
- **Names in Russian letters** (`пример.рф`, `+.госуслуги.рф`, a link to one) are taken; they are kept as punycode, the form the core compares. A link with an IPv6 address in brackets and a name with a trailing dot are taken too.
- A line of no kind refuses the save and stays in the box to be fixed. A list over 4 MB is refused, and what was typed is kept: before, it was saved and never used.
- The blocks say when the auto-switch mode sets them aside, and the three blocks line up.

## Auto-switch: on, observe only, tunnel only

- **On:** the verdicts are applied, as before.
- **Observe only:** everything goes direct, the presets and the lists included; the detector measures it all.
- **Tunnel only:** everything goes through awg and awg2, Always direct included.
- The detector checks and records in every mode. A switch closes the open connections the new mode sends another way, so they reconnect by the new rules within a second.
- The header, the settings, the verdicts and the overview show the same mode, and say when the verdicts are recorded but not applied.

## Second tunnel

- **Presets are edited, deleted and added** in a dialog: a name, a description and lines, as the lists take them. A new preset is switched on at once.
- **Restore built-in presets…** puts the shipped presets back, deleted or edited ones included; your own presets stay.
- Adding or deleting a preset needs no core restart.
- A second `.conf` the core cannot use is refused with the reason, instead of being shown as attached while left out of the core's config.

## Live

- **A row can be picked**: it holds its place while the others move. **Right-click** opens a menu: send the whole domain, the name, the address or the program **Direct**, **Via the tunnel**, **Via the second tunnel**, **To a preset** or **Forbid**, and **File location** opens the program's folder. The line leaves the lists that would route it otherwise, and the open connections it moves are moved.
- **Closed connections and failures are kept for the core's whole run** (the last 100,000 of each), not for ten minutes. A restart of the core starts the history over.
- A long history sorts without freezing the page.

## Settings, verdicts, overview, logs

- **DNS test:** finds whether a DoH server wants `/dns-query` and puts the address that answers in the box. A refused DNS save keeps what was typed and says why in the page's language; "the core restarts" is said only when it does.
- The terms offer only what the settings take (the blocked re-check offered 30 days, which was always refused).
- **Verdicts:** the filter finds a whole domain by its `+.` and a Russian name by its letters, and keeps working as the table refreshes. A verdict waiting for its name to be used again says "when next used", not "due now". **Reset all verdicts** works with the service stopped: it is done when the service starts.
- **Overview:** a `.conf` loaded with the service stopped is shown as loaded; the tunnel's DNS is the one in use; the recent events show the newest lines.
- **Logs:** a log just rotated goes on into its previous copy, so the lines before a restart stay in sight. With "Follow the end" off, the line being read stays in place; selected text is no longer cleared by the refresh.

## Fixes

- A new site whose check was cut short (the core restarting, the network changing) is checked again; before, it waited for its next connection.
- **Everything via tunnel** (the verdict reset) is done only once the emptied memory is saved; before, a failed save let every verdict come back at the next start.
- With thousands of connections open (a torrent client), the core's connection list grew past what was read, and the detector and Live stopped working. It is read up to 64 MB now.
- The tray's tooltip is no longer cut short in Russian.
